children: is no longer just building the digital dollar. It is building the network that could move it.
the public mainnet launch of Arc, an open Layer 1 blockchain designed for financial markets, real-time payments, and AI-driven transactions.
The big deal? Wall Street institutions are helping secure it.
The launch brings major financial institutions into the network’s founding validator cohort, including BlackRock
, the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC), Visa
The firm said Arc went live with more than 100 applications and over 100 institutional and ecosystem builders.
Arc is built around Circle's USDC
stablecoin, which had more than $74B in circulation at launch. Unlike many blockchains, transaction fees are paid in USDC rather than a volatile native token.
The network also targets sub-second finality, allowing transactions to settle almost instantly.
“USDC was step one. Arc is the network built for what comes next,” Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire said.

The opportunity extends beyond payments. Circle’s StableFX is designed to support 24/7 cross-currency settlement, while its native payments integration is designed to support tokenized assets, trading, lending, and AI agents that can execute economic tasks on behalf of users and businesses.
BlackRock’s global head of digital assets, Robbie Mitchnick, said purpose-built blockchains could help accelerate stablecoin and payment adoption.

The company also completed the initial mint of 10B ARC tokens this week. However, the company said this is a technical milestone, not a commitment to launch the token publicly. A transition toward proof of stake is being explored for 2027.

title: Circle launches Arc blockchain with Wall Street giants
